mechanism_narrative: A rise in GDP above its 6-month moving average indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during expansion periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, which in turn drives down S&P 500 prices over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 5% indicates a weakening labor market, leading to decreased consumer spending and lower S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during recession periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) both increase, it indicates a strong demand for goods and services, leading to higher S&P 500 prices over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when both housing starts and retail sales are increasing (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 3-month moving average indicates increased supply, leading to higher S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during expansion periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is above 190, it signals an inflationary environment, leading to higher S&P 500 prices over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the federal funds rate is below 4% and the consumer price index is above 190 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% indicates a strong labor market, leading to higher S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during expansion periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 4.5%, it indicates a strong demand for goods and services, leading to higher S&P 500 prices over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when payroll employment is increasing and the federal funds rate is below 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05).
